title: The Born–Haber cycle for sodium chloride
caption: From the elements, sodium and chlorine are atomised (+107, +122), sodium is ionised (+496) and chlorine gains an electron (−349). The gaseous ions then form the lattice. Since the two routes to NaCl(s) must agree, −411 = 107 + 122 + 496 − 349 + ΔlattH, so ΔlattH = −787 kJ mol⁻¹.
alt: Enthalpy level diagram rising from Na(s) + ½Cl₂(g) through atomisation and ionisation, falling for the electron affinity, then a long downward arrow for lattice formation to NaCl(s), which is 411 below the start.
description: Up +107 to Na(g); up +122 to Na(g) + Cl(g); up +496 to Na⁺(g) + e⁻ + Cl(g).
Down by the lattice enthalpy to NaCl(s), which is −411 below the start (the enthalpy of formation).
So the lattice enthalpy is −787 kJ mol⁻¹.
